archetype.name: Lottery Team (outplayed at 5-on-5)
archetype.definition: A club whose last-place-range record is matched by its underlying play: it is out-chanced, out-shot and out-finished most nights, with goaltending keeping the score closer than the territory suggests.

report.headline: A 98-point team last year now loses the puck, the chances, and the scoreboard
report.take:
Philadelphia is 6-11-6, 28th of 32 on the site, and the record is no accident. The Flyers have just 2.3 goals a game, 31st in the league, and they give up 3.35. The 5-on-5 numbers say the same thing in a different way: a 44.1% share of expected goals and a 46% share of shot attempts, both 28th. They put 24.6 shots a game on net, 29th, against a league average of 27.4. This is a team that spends its nights defending.

The drop from last season is the story. In 2025-26 this group went 43-27-12 for 98 points, won four playoff games, controlled 50.6% of expected goals and ranked 9th in goals against. The goaltending is not the culprit this time. Team GSAx is +1.4, 15th and slightly above the league mean, a far cry from the -45.8 of 2024-25. Joseph Woll has carried that number at +4.6 with a .902 save percentage. Dan Vladar has given back -3.2 at .877. Most of the trouble sits further up the ice. Trevor Zegras leads the forwards in minutes at 18.47 a night, yet his line gets only 38.3% of expected goals. Jamie Drysdale's pair is at 41.1% in more than 23 minutes. Opposing defensemen score against this team more than their averages predict (rank 27). The forwards grade D- and the blueline D.

The numbers hide less than you'd hope. The skaters shoot 9.4%, 28th and two points below the league's 11.4%, and the 5-on-5 PDO of 97.7 says some finishing will come back. But a low-volume team with a bad chance share doesn't turn into a .500 club when shooting normalizes. Pts vs Goal Diff of +0.6 shows they haven't been especially unlucky in close games either. The -24 differential is close to an honest one. Matvei Michkov is the outlier in the other direction: 11 goals on 36 shots, the only forward ranked inside the top quarter of his tab.

There is a little light. October was 3-11, including a nine-game losing streak. November is 3-5 with 3 goals a game, and the last five went 2-1-2 for a .600 points percentage, beating the season rate on both scoring and prevention. That looks like a team climbing from awful toward merely below average. A 64-point pace gets better from here, but not enough to matter in a Metropolitan led by Carolina and New Jersey.

strengths.title: Woll is holding the crease together
strengths.body: Joseph Woll has a .902 save percentage and +4.6 GSAx over 11 starts, 25th of 71 on the goalie tab. That is why team GSAx sits slightly above the league despite Vladar's -3.2. On a team allowing 28 shots a game, every start that goes to Woll rather than Vladar is worth something real. Woll's level looks sustainable; the open question is whether the split moves his way.

strengths.title: Michkov is the scoring threat
strengths.body: Matvei Michkov has 11 of the forwards' 37 goals and the group's best Game Score at 12.1, ranking 28th of 132 right wings. He also has 7 power-play points. His goals have come on only 36 shots, so the finishing rate will cool. His -12 and 42% xGF share show he is also caught up in the team's territorial problems.

strengths.title: Depth lines win their minutes
strengths.body: Some of the lower-minute forwards drive play better than the top of the lineup. Denver Barkey sits at 55.3% xGF with 10 points in 19 games, and Noah Cates is at 52.6% and even on the season. Both are among the few skaters on the right side of the chance share. That points to a lineup where heavier usage of the players who win their shifts could help.

concerns.title: Badly outplayed at five-on-five
concerns.body: The 44.1% expected-goals share and 46% Corsi both rank 28th, and the gaps to the league are wide. This is the root of the season, and it is a sharp break from last year's 50.6%. Shot volume backs it up: 24.6 shots for against 28 allowed a game. Until the top lines tilt the ice, wins will stay scarce.

concerns.title: An offense with no volume or finish
concerns.body: At 2.3 goals a game Philadelphia is 31st, 0.87 under the league rate. It shoots 9.4% on a low shot count, and the power play converts 17.3%, 27th. Some shooting regression upward is likely. With this few shots, though, even league-average finishing leaves the attack in the bottom third.

concerns.title: Top minutes are underwater
concerns.body: The players eating the most ice are losing their matchups. Zegras is at 38.3% xGF in 18.47 minutes, Drysdale at 41.1% in 23.12, and Cam York sits 220th of 259 defensemen at -9. Opposing defensemen produce above their averages against this group (rank 27). That points to a blueline that struggles to defend the point and to break out cleanly.

trend.note: A 3-11 October, with a nine-game skid, gave way to a 3-5 November at 3 goals a game. The last five went 2-1-2 for a .600 points percentage. It is improvement from a very low floor, still with a negative differential.

weekAhead.headline: Buffalo at home, then two road games against overachievers
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with the best chance of the three. Buffalo is 8-8-4 and 22nd on the site. It owns the league's worst all-situations PDO and a .873 team save percentage. Its defense allows centers and forwards well beyond their averages, ranking 32nd and 29th. The Sabres do push the puck, at a 53% Corsi with an A- blueline, so this won't be a territorial win. It is a game where Philadelphia's low shooting percentage has its best shot at correcting.

Then comes the road. Ottawa (13-6-2) and Montreal (12-4-4) are both better teams, and both are riding 5-on-5 PDOs of 103.2 with strong Pts vs Goal Diff marks. Montreal's +3.6 is first in the league. Both also have bottom-two power plays, which takes away one way they could punish the Flyers' middling PK. A split of the two road games would be a good outcome; the likeliest result is one win in three.

keyMatchups.title: Flyers centers versus Buffalo's middle
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo allows centers +0.76 points above expectation a game, the worst mark in the league. Its goaltending sits 24th in GSAx. Zegras, Dvorak and Barkey should find room. This is the game for the 9.4% shooting to tick up.

keyMatchups.title: Ottawa shuts down centers, not wingers
keyMatchups.body: Ottawa ranks 3rd at holding centers under their averages but 22nd against wingers. That points the Flyers' attack toward Michkov and Martone on the flanks. The Senators' 53.1% xGF share means Philadelphia will be chasing the play. Their 11.5% power play, worst in the league, softens penalty trouble.

keyMatchups.title: Montreal's goalie and its luck
keyMatchups.body: Montreal's goalies are +10.2 GSAx, 5th, and the club leads the league in points beyond its goal differential. That makes a low-volume shooting team's night harder. The Canadiens' run of close-game fortune is the kind that fades, but probably not in one game.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in Ottawa and Montreal: Woll's +4.6 GSAx against Vladar's -3.2 is the biggest lever this team controls on the road.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the scoring to tick up from here. A 9.4% shooting rate on a team with Michkov finishing well is low, and November's 3 goals a game is closer to the true level than October's 2.07. That lifts the club off its 64-point, 21-win pace. The expected-goals share caps how far it can climb. At 44% this is not a .500 team, and the save percentage is roughly average, so no hidden goaltending upside offsets it beyond giving Woll more starts. With 59 games left and a five-point hole to sixth in the division before even counting the leaders, the realistic target is respectability, not a playoff chase.

I'd project a finish around 26 to 30 wins and 66 to 76 points, with goals per game settling in the 2.6 to 2.9 range. Last season's turnaround came with a 100.8 PDO and a positive chance share. Neither is present now, so a repeat would need a genuine change in how the top two lines and the top pair play.

confidence.note: 23 games is a modest sample, but the chance share, shot volume and record all point the same way.
